title: Your Truck Is Nine Years Old
kidsText: Your old truck still runs. Keep it, buy a used one, or get a new one?
adultText: The old one still runs, but the new ones have heated seats. Keep it, pay cash for a used one, or finance new?

options.label: Keep the old truck
options.kidsText: Keep driving it. It still works.
options.adultText: It still runs. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy a used truck for cash
options.kidsText: Pay $4,000 cash for a used one.
options.adultText: A three-year-old truck, paid in full. No monthly payment.

options.label: Finance a new truck
options.kidsText: Take a loan. Pay $380 every month.
options.adultText: The dealer's loan: 12,000 at 380 a month. Heated seats included.

title: Family Beach Week
kidsText: A week at the beach for the whole family. Go, or stay home this year?
adultText: Seven nights, four people, one rented house by the ocean. Memories are not a monthly bill, but the trip is.

options.label: Stay home this year
options.kidsText: Stay home and keep the money.
options.adultText: A week of day trips instead. Nothing changes.

options.label: Book the beach house
options.kidsText: Pay $2,500 for the trip.
options.adultText: Pay 2,500 in cash for the week.

title: Big Screen and Sound System
kidsText: A giant TV and big speakers. Keep your old TV, pay cash, or pay a little each month?
adultText: Wall-sized television and speakers you can feel. The store offers no-money-down financing.

options.label: Keep the old TV
options.kidsText: Your old TV still works. Keep it.
options.adultText: It still works. Nothing changes.

options.label: Pay cash
options.kidsText: Pay $1,800 cash.
options.adultText: Pay 1,800 in cash. No monthly payment.

options.label: Finance it
options.kidsText: Pay $90 every month for a long time.
options.adultText: No money down, 90 a month on 1,800 of principal.

title: Streaming Bundle
kidsText: Four streaming apps in one bundle for $60 a month. Sign up, or skip it?
adultText: Four streaming services in one bundle, 60 a month, cancel any time. Will you?

options.label: Skip it
options.kidsText: Skip it and keep your money.
options.adultText: Nothing changes.

options.label: Subscribe for 60 a month
options.kidsText: Pay $60 every month until you cancel.
options.adultText: A subscription liability of 60 a month. REPAY cancels it at no cost.

title: Tax Refund
kidsText: A $2,000 tax refund! Spend it, invest it, or pay off debt?
adultText: A 2,000 refund lands in your account. Spend it, invest it in an index fund, or pay down your most expensive loan?

options.label: Spend it
options.kidsText: Buy stuff with the whole $2,000.
options.adultText: A shopping weekend. The 2,000 is gone by Monday.

options.label: Invest it in an index fund
options.kidsText: Put the $2,000 in an index fund. It grows every month.
options.adultText: Index fund: grows 4 percent a month and pays out 1 percent of its value each Payday.

options.label: Pay down your biggest loan
options.kidsText: Pay $2,000 toward your loan with the biggest payment.
options.adultText: Pays up to 2,000 toward the loan with the highest monthly payment. Mortgages are not loans here.

title: New SUV Lease Offer
kidsText: A shiny new SUV with a low monthly price. Keep your car, buy used, or lease?
adultText: Zero down and 360 a month for three years. At the end you own nothing. Keep your car, buy used with cash, or lease?

options.label: Keep your car
options.kidsText: Your car works fine. Keep it.
options.adultText: It is paid off and runs well. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy a used SUV for cash
options.kidsText: Pay $6,000 cash for a used SUV.
options.adultText: A four-year-old SUV for 6,000 cash. It already lost most of its value, so you do not lose it.

options.label: Lease the new SUV
options.kidsText: Pay $360 every month. You give it back later.
options.adultText: 360 a month on a 13,000 lease balance. Paying it off early means paying the whole balance.

title: Your Car Hits 150,000 Miles
kidsText: Your car is getting old. Keep driving it, buy used, or get a new one?
adultText: The odometer rolls past 150,000. It still starts every morning. Keep it, buy a used one with cash, or finance new?

options.label: Keep driving it
options.kidsText: Keep driving it. It still starts.
options.adultText: Change the oil and keep going. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy a used car for cash
options.kidsText: Pay $7,000 cash for a newer used car.
options.adultText: A five-year-old sedan for 7,000 cash. No payment.

options.label: Finance a new car
options.kidsText: Take a loan. Pay $520 every month.
options.adultText: 26,000 financed at 520 a month. It loses a fifth of its value when you drive it off the lot.

title: New Bike Season
kidsText: Bikes are on sale. Keep your old bike, buy a used one, or get a new e-bike?
adultText: Spring sales are on. Keep riding the old bike, buy a used one, or get a new electric bike?

options.label: Keep your old bike
options.kidsText: Pump up the tires and keep riding.
options.adultText: New tires and a tune-up you do yourself. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy a used bike
options.kidsText: Pay $200 for a used bike.
options.adultText: A lightly used bike from a neighbor for 200.

options.label: Buy a new e-bike
options.kidsText: Pay $1,500 for a new electric bike.
options.adultText: A new e-bike for 1,500 cash. Fun, fast, and worth half that in a year.

title: Motorcycle for the Summer
kidsText: A motorcycle would be fun. Skip it, buy used, or take a loan for a new one?
adultText: Summer is coming and a friend is selling. Skip it, buy his used bike for cash, or finance a new one?

options.label: Skip it
options.kidsText: Skip it. Keep your money.
options.adultText: Ride with friends on their bikes. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy the used motorcycle
options.kidsText: Pay $4,000 cash for a used motorcycle.
options.adultText: Your friend's bike for 4,000 cash. No payment.

options.label: Finance a new motorcycle
options.kidsText: Take a loan. Pay $250 every month.
options.adultText: 9,000 financed at 250 a month. Fun on sunny days, a payment every day.

title: Designer Sneakers Drop
kidsText: Famous sneakers come out today. Skip them, buy one pair, or use a store card?
adultText: A limited release everyone is posting about. Skip it, buy one pair with cash, or open a store card for three pairs?

options.label: Skip the drop
options.kidsText: Your shoes are fine. Skip it.
options.adultText: Your shoes are fine. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy one pair
options.kidsText: Pay $300 for one pair.
options.adultText: One pair for 300 cash. Worn twice, they are just shoes.

options.label: Three pairs on a store card
options.kidsText: Pay $45 every month for a long time.
options.adultText: Three pairs on a store card: 900 owed at 45 a month.

title: Wardrobe Refresh
kidsText: Your clothes look a little old. Keep them, shop thrift, or buy brand names?
adultText: New job, new season, same old clothes. Keep them, hit the thrift store, or shop the mall brands?

options.label: Keep what you have
options.kidsText: Your clothes still fit. Keep them.
options.adultText: They still fit and nobody is keeping score. Nothing changes.

options.label: Shop thrift stores
options.kidsText: Pay $200 at the thrift store.
options.adultText: A full refresh for 200 at thrift and consignment stores.

options.label: Buy brand names
options.kidsText: Pay $1,200 for new brand-name clothes.
options.adultText: 1,200 at the mall. Worth a tenth of that the day you cut the tags.

title: Style Box Subscription
kidsText: New clothes mailed to you every month. Skip it, or pay $70 a month?
adultText: A stylist picks clothes and mails a box every month. 70 a month until you cancel. Sign up?

options.label: Skip it
options.kidsText: Skip it and keep your money.
options.adultText: Nothing changes.

options.label: Subscribe for 70 a month
options.kidsText: Pay $70 every month until you cancel.
options.adultText: A subscription of 70 a month. REPAY cancels it at no cost.

title: Winter Coat Sale
kidsText: Your coat is old. Keep it, buy one on sale, or get a fancy brand?
adultText: The zipper sticks, but the coat is warm. Keep it, buy a sale coat, or get the brand everyone wears?

options.label: Keep your coat
options.kidsText: Fix the zipper and keep it.
options.adultText: Fix the zipper for a few dollars. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy a coat on sale
options.kidsText: Pay $100 for a warm coat on sale.
options.adultText: A warm coat for 100 at an end-of-season sale.

options.label: Buy the fancy brand
options.kidsText: Pay $600 for the fancy coat.
options.adultText: 600 for the logo. Just as warm as the sale coat.

title: New Phone Comes Out
kidsText: A new phone just came out. Keep yours, pay cash, or pay each month?
adultText: Your phone works, but the new one has a better camera. Keep yours, pay cash, or take the carrier's payment plan?

options.label: Keep your phone
options.kidsText: Your phone still works. Keep it.
options.adultText: New battery, same phone. Nothing changes.

options.label: Pay cash
options.kidsText: Pay $1,000 cash for the new phone.
options.adultText: 1,000 cash. Worth half that in a year.

options.label: Payment plan
options.kidsText: Pay $50 every month for the phone.
options.adultText: 1,000 on the carrier plan at 50 a month. It feels free. It is not.

title: Gaming Console
kidsText: A new game system! Skip it, buy it, or buy it with a monthly game pass?
adultText: The new console is out. Skip it, buy it with cash, or buy it plus the monthly game pass?

options.label: Skip it
options.kidsText: Play your old games. Skip it.
options.adultText: Your old games still work. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy the console
options.kidsText: Pay $500 for the game system.
options.adultText: 500 cash. Next year's model will make it look old.

options.label: Console plus game pass
options.kidsText: Pay $500 now and $20 every month.
options.adultText: 500 cash plus a game pass at 20 a month until you cancel.

title: Laptop Upgrade
kidsText: Your computer is slow. Keep it, buy a fixed-up one, or get the best one?
adultText: The old laptop is slow but works. Keep it, buy a refurbished one, or finance the top model?

options.label: Keep your laptop
options.kidsText: Clean it up and keep using it.
options.adultText: Clear the junk and add memory yourself. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy refurbished
options.kidsText: Pay $400 for a fixed-up laptop.
options.adultText: A refurbished business laptop for 400 with a warranty.

options.label: Finance the top model
options.kidsText: Pay $110 every month for the best laptop.
options.adultText: 2,400 financed at 110 a month. Fast, beautiful, and outdated in three years.

title: Smart Home Gadgets
kidsText: Talking speakers and smart lights. Skip them, buy them, or buy them with a monthly plan?
adultText: Smart speakers, lights, and a doorbell camera. Skip it, buy the gear, or add the monitoring plan?

options.label: Skip it
options.kidsText: Flip the light switch yourself. Skip it.
options.adultText: Light switches still work. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy the gadgets
options.kidsText: Pay $300 for the gadgets.
options.adultText: 300 for the starter kit.

options.label: Gadgets plus monitoring
options.kidsText: Pay $300 now and $30 every month.
options.adultText: 300 for the kit plus a monitoring plan at 30 a month until you cancel.

title: Gym Membership
kidsText: Join a gym? Exercise outside for free, join a gym, or join a fancy club?
adultText: January energy. Run outside for free, join the basic gym, or the club with the smoothie bar?

options.label: Exercise outside
options.kidsText: Run and play outside for free.
options.adultText: Free trails and a jump rope. Nothing changes.

options.label: Basic gym for 40 a month
options.kidsText: Pay $40 every month until you cancel.
options.adultText: A subscription of 40 a month. REPAY cancels it at no cost.

options.label: Fancy club for 120 a month
options.kidsText: Pay $120 every month until you cancel.
options.adultText: A subscription of 120 a month. Most members stop going by March.

title: Meal Kit Delivery
kidsText: Dinner boxes mailed to your house. Cook at home, or pay every month for boxes?
adultText: Pre-portioned dinners on your porch. Keep cooking from the store, two nights a week, or every night?

options.label: Keep cooking
options.kidsText: Cook with food from the store.
options.adultText: Grocery store and a meal plan. Nothing changes.

options.label: Two nights a week
options.kidsText: Pay $120 every month until you cancel.
options.adultText: A subscription of 120 a month for two dinners a week.

options.label: Every night
options.kidsText: Pay $300 every month until you cancel.
options.adultText: A subscription of 300 a month. Convenient, and more than twice the cost of groceries.

title: Phone Plan Upgrade
kidsText: The phone store says get the best plan. Keep yours, or pay $30 more a month?
adultText: The premium plan adds hotspot data and a streaming bonus for 30 more a month. Keep your plan or upgrade?

options.label: Keep your plan
options.kidsText: Keep the plan you have.
options.adultText: Wi-Fi at home covers it. Nothing changes.

options.label: Upgrade for 30 a month
options.kidsText: Pay $30 more every month.
options.adultText: A subscription of 30 a month. REPAY cancels it at no cost.

title: Food Delivery Habit
kidsText: Food brought to your door. Skip it, join for $10 a month, or order every week?
adultText: Free delivery with a membership. Skip it, join for 10 a month, or join and order takeout every week?

options.label: Skip it
options.kidsText: Eat at home and keep your money.
options.adultText: Nothing changes.

options.label: Join for 10 a month
options.kidsText: Pay $10 every month.
options.adultText: A membership of 10 a month. REPAY cancels it at no cost.

options.label: Order every week
options.kidsText: Pay $160 every month for weekly takeout.
options.adultText: Membership plus weekly family takeout: 160 a month until you cancel.

title: Music and Audiobook Apps
kidsText: Music apps! Use the free one, pay for one app, or get the family bundle?
adultText: Use the free version with ads, pay for one app at 10 a month, or get the family bundle at 30?

options.label: Use the free version
options.kidsText: Listen for free with ads.
options.adultText: A few ads never hurt anyone. Nothing changes.

options.label: One app for 10 a month
options.kidsText: Pay $10 every month.
options.adultText: A subscription of 10 a month.

options.label: Family bundle for 30 a month
options.kidsText: Pay $30 every month.
options.adultText: A subscription of 30 a month for music, audiobooks, and podcasts.

title: Bigger House
kidsText: A bigger house is for sale. Stay in your home, or move to the big one?
adultText: Four bedrooms, a three-car garage, and a bigger payment. Stay where you are, or move up?

options.label: Stay where you are
options.kidsText: Your home is big enough. Stay.
options.adultText: Your house fits your family. Nothing changes.

options.label: Move to the bigger house
options.kidsText: Pay $5,000 now and $450 more every month.
options.adultText: 5,000 toward the down payment and 450 more a month in mortgage, taxes, and insurance on 50,000 more debt.

title: Cousin's Destination Wedding
kidsText: Your cousin is getting married far away. Send a card, or fly there?
adultText: A beach wedding two time zones away. Send a gift and a video message, fly in for the weekend, or stay the whole week?

options.label: Send a card and a video
options.kidsText: Send a card and a happy video.
options.adultText: A heartfelt card and a toast by video. Nothing changes.

options.label: Fly in for the weekend
options.kidsText: Pay $1,800 for the trip.
options.adultText: Flights, hotel, and a gift for 1,800 cash.

options.label: Stay the whole week
options.kidsText: Pay $4,000 for a whole week there.
options.adultText: A week at the resort for 4,000 cash.

title: Boat Show Deal
kidsText: A boat for the lake! Skip it, buy a used one, or take a loan for a new one?
adultText: The boat show has deals. Skip it, buy a used fishing boat with cash, or finance a new pontoon?

options.label: Skip it
options.kidsText: Fish from the dock. Skip the boat.
options.adultText: Rent a boat twice a summer. Nothing changes.

options.label: Buy a used boat
options.kidsText: Pay $8,000 cash for a used boat.
options.adultText: A used fishing boat and trailer for 8,000 cash.

options.label: Finance a new pontoon
options.kidsText: Take a loan. Pay $400 every month.
options.adultText: 30,000 financed at 400 a month, plus a boat that loses value every season.

title: Neighbor's House Fire
kidsText: Your neighbor's house caught fire. Everyone is safe. How will you help?
adultText: Your neighbors lost their kitchen to a fire. Everyone is safe. Help with your hands, or with your wallet too?

options.label: Bring meals and help clean
options.kidsText: Bring food and help clean up. Your time is a gift.
options.adultText: Meals for a week and a Saturday hauling debris. Generosity is not only money. Nothing changes.

options.label: Give $500
options.kidsText: Give $500 to help them.
options.adultText: 500 toward a hotel and new clothes for the kids.

options.label: Give $1,500
options.kidsText: Give $1,500 to help them.
options.adultText: 1,500 to cover their insurance deductible.

title: Work Bonus
kidsText: You got a $3,000 bonus at work! Spend it, invest it, or pay off debt?
adultText: A 3,000 bonus for a great year. Spend it, invest it in an index fund, or pay down your most expensive loan?

options.label: Spend it
options.kidsText: Buy fun stuff with all $3,000.
options.adultText: A new TV and a weekend away. The 3,000 is gone.

options.label: Invest it in an index fund
options.kidsText: Put the $3,000 in an index fund. It grows every month.
options.adultText: Index fund: grows 4 percent a month and pays out 1 percent of its value each Payday.

options.label: Pay down your biggest loan
options.kidsText: Pay $3,000 toward your loan with the biggest payment.
options.adultText: Pays up to 3,000 toward the loan with the highest monthly payment. Mortgages are not loans here.

title: Inheritance
kidsText: A great-aunt left you $10,000. Give some and invest, pay off debt, or spend it?
adultText: Your great-aunt left you 10,000 and a note: do some good with it. Give and invest, pay down debt, or spend it?

options.label: Give 1,000 and invest 9,000
options.kidsText: Give $1,000 away and put $9,000 in an index fund.
options.adultText: 1,000 to her church and 9,000 in an index fund that grows 4 percent a month and pays out 1 percent.

options.label: Pay down your biggest loan
options.kidsText: Pay $10,000 toward your loan with the biggest payment.
options.adultText: Pays up to 10,000 toward the loan with the highest monthly payment. Mortgages are not loans here.

options.label: Spend it
options.kidsText: Spend all $10,000 on fun things.
options.adultText: A new car down payment and a big trip. The 10,000 is gone.

title: Garage Sale Money
kidsText: Your garage sale made $400! Save it, spend it, or keep it as cash?
adultText: You cleared the garage and made 400. Put it in savings, spend it on a night out, or keep it in your wallet?

options.label: Put it in savings
options.kidsText: Put $400 in savings. It grows a tiny bit every month.
options.adultText: Savings: grows 1 percent a month and stays there for emergencies.

options.label: Spend it
options.kidsText: Spend all $400 on a fun night out.
options.adultText: A nice dinner and a movie. The 400 is gone.

options.label: Keep it as cash
options.kidsText: Keep the $400 as cash for later.
options.adultText: 400 more cash on hand.

title: Overtime Paycheck
kidsText: You worked extra and earned $1,500 more! Save it, spend it, or pay debt?
adultText: A month of overtime adds 1,500. Build your emergency fund, buy gadgets, or pay down your biggest loan?

options.label: Build your emergency fund
options.kidsText: Put $1,500 in savings for surprises.
options.adultText: Savings: grows 1 percent a month and is there when the furnace dies.

options.label: Buy gadgets
options.kidsText: Spend all $1,500 on gadgets.
options.adultText: New headphones, a tablet, and a smartwatch. The 1,500 is gone.

options.label: Pay down your biggest loan
options.kidsText: Pay $1,500 toward your loan with the biggest payment.
options.adultText: Pays up to 1,500 toward the loan with the highest monthly payment. Mortgages are not loans here.
